author: Kate Sherman
title: Mobile business gets license revoked after numerous incomplete work - NewsBreak
text:
By Kate Sherman Michael Hanich ,
1 hours ago
MOBILE, Ala. (WKRG) — A Mobile business has officially lost its business license.
Bertha Makes Landfall in Louisiana, Gusty Winds & Surf Continues Mobile City Council unanimously voted to revoke the license tied to Window Depot and All Weather Roofing after more than 100 customers reported paying for work that was never completed.
For the customers who say they paid thousands of dollars and were left waiting for work that never happened, this vote marks another major development in the case.
Mobile City Council unanimously voted to revoke the business license tied to Window Depot and All Weather Roofing.
Council members said the business had previously indicated it would voluntarily surrender its license. But after that didn’t happen, they said they had no choice but to move forward with revoking it.
Police say 108 people have now come forward claiming they paid for home improvement projects that were never completed, totaling nearly $1 million in reported losses.
“I don’t know of any time in the City of Mobile where we’ve had a situation like this,” Curtis Graves of Director of Public Safety. “This is uncharted territory for a lot of us, unfortunately. I think business owners are, in general, good business owners, and they understand that in order to stay in business, you have to treat customers with respect and dignity”
Graves says investigators are still actively working the case and have not yet turned the investigation over to the district attorney’s office. He also says revoking this business license does not automatically prevent those involved from applying for another business license in the future.
